definition: not allowing passage; unable to be affected
memoryTip: Im-pervious: nothing can pierce through (water, criticism).
correctPassage: The coating is nearly impervious to water and salt air.
wrongPassages: The sponge was impervious to the spill and soaked through within seconds.
He tried to impervious the callers by parking them on mute without answering.
Critics found her open to every critique, utterly impervious and quick to revise.

definition: not able to be defended or maintained
memoryTip: Can’t tenably hold it — the argument collapses; position is indefensible.
correctPassage: Once the data were corrected, the original hypothesis became untenable.
wrongPassages: The plan was untenable because every risk had already been eliminated and every owner named.
Judges called the ruling untenable because it carefully weighed both sides and cited law.
After independent replications matched every prediction, the hypothesis no longer looked untenable.

memoryTip: Ubi = where (Latin) — seems to be everywhere you look.
correctPassage: Smartphones are now so ubiquitous that many public spaces assume constant connectivity.
wrongPassages: Rotary phones are ubiquitous here: one sits on every modern classroom desk.
The orchid is ubiquitous—only a single wild specimen has ever been found.
He kept his ubiquitous diary in one locked drawer no visitor ever saw.

memoryTip: De-funct: function stopped — dead, no longer running.
correctPassage: The defunct railway line has been converted into a walking path.
wrongPassages: The defunct clinic still books patients seven days a week and posts daily wait times.
Investors poured capital into the defunct startup after record quarterly growth.
She marked the live feed defunct while thousands watched the stream in real time.

definition: a person who criticizes or disparages someone or something
memoryTip: De-tract: pulls reputation down — a critic who knocks you.
correctPassage: Even the project’s fiercest detractor admitted the design was elegant.
wrongPassages: The lead sponsor acted as chief detractor, funding the tour and praising every stop.
She hired a detractor to write glowing blurbs for the dust jacket.
His lifelong detractor never missed a premiere and always led the standing ovation.
